Dutch

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from German Biologie, from Ancient Greek βιολογία (biología). This is a compound of βίος (bíos, “life”) and λόγος (lógos, “reason”) with the suffix -ία (-ía) (forms abstracta), equivalent to bio- +‎ -logie.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˌbi.oː.loːˈɣi/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Hyphenation: bio‧lo‧gie
  • Rhymes: -i

Noun

[edit]

biologie f (uncountable, no diminutive)

  1. biology (science of living matter)

Derived terms

[edit]
  • biologieles
  • biologisch
  • celbiologie
  • evolutiebiologie
  • microbiologie
  • ontwikkelingsbiologie
  • veldbiologie

Related terms

[edit]
  • bioloog

Descendants

[edit]
  • Afrikaans: biologie
  • → Indonesian: biologi

References

[edit]
  • “biologie” in Woordenlijst Nederlandse Taal – Officiële Spelling, Nederlandse Taalunie. [the official spelling word list for the Dutch language]

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

As a French word, coined by Jean-Baptiste Lamarck in 1802. Possibly formed as bio- +‎ -logie. Possibly borrowed from German Biologie or New Latin biologia. In any case, derived from Ancient Greek βίος (bíos, “bio-, life”) + -λογία (-logía, “-logy, branch of study, to speak”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /bjɔ.lɔ.ʒi/
  • Audio (Paris):(file)
  • Audio (Paris):(file)
  • Audio (Switzerland (Valais)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Paris)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Toulouse)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Saint-Étienne)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)
  • Rhymes: -i
  • Homophone: biologies
  • Hyphenation: bio‧lo‧gie

Noun

[edit]

biologie f (plural biologies)

  1. biology

Derived terms

[edit]
  • microbiologie
  • scotobiologie

Related terms

[edit]
  • biologique
  • biologiste

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Persian: بیولوژی (biyoloži)
  • → Romanian: biologie
  • → Turkish: biyoloji

Further reading

[edit]
  • “biologie”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012
